Economy & Trading
Learn how Albion\'s economy works through trading, transporting goods, managing islands and earning silver.
Gathering Basics
Learn the fundamentals of collecting wood, ore, fiber, hide and stone.

Gather resources from resource nodes found throughout Albion. Each resource type requires its matching gathering tool: an axe for wood, a pickaxe for ore, a sickle for fiber, a skinning knife for hide and a stone hammer for stone. Higher-tier resources require higher-tier gathering levels and tools. Gathering resources grants fame toward the relevant gathering profession.

Start in safe zones while learning the resource locations and tool requirements. Upgrade your tools as your gathering level increases. Use a mount to carry resources, watch your carry weight and return to a city before you become overloaded. Consider gathering resources that are in demand on the marketplace.
Gathering Tips
Improve gathering efficiency with the right equipment, food, routes and preparation.

Gathering efficiency depends on your gathering level, equipment, food and the resource nodes available in each zone. Gathering gear provides bonuses related to a particular resource. Food such as Pork Pie can increase gathering yield, while gathering tools determine which resource tiers you can collect.

Wear gathering equipment for the resource you intend to collect. Plan a route through areas with several resource nodes and avoid spending too much time travelling between them. Keep an eye on your inventory weight and market prices. Do not risk expensive equipment when gathering in dangerous areas unless you can afford to replace it.
Gathering Specialization
Understand gathering fame, profession levels and specialization progression.

Each gathering profession has its own progression. Gathering a resource grants fame toward that profession and unlocks access to higher resource tiers as you advance. Further specialization improves your efficiency in that resource profession and can increase your gathering yield.

Focus on the resource types you actually want to gather instead of spreading your progress across every profession. Higher specialization is especially useful when gathering regularly. Check the Destiny Board to understand the requirements for the next level and plan your gathering around your goals.
Dangerous Zones
Learn how to gather in Red and Black Zones while managing the risk of PvP.

Red and Black Zones contain full-loot PvP risks. Other players can attack you, and being killed in these areas can result in losing the equipment and resources you are carrying. These zones can also contain more valuable and higher-tier resources. Red Zones show hostile player information, while Black Zones are especially dangerous because players can attack without the same hostile-flag warning system.

Use an inexpensive gathering set and a mount suited to your load. Watch the local player indicators in Red Zones and check your surroundings frequently. In Black Zones, avoid predictable routes and crowded areas. Keep escape abilities available, do not overfill your inventory and never carry more value than you are prepared to lose.
Crafting Basics
Learn how to craft weapons, armor, tools, consumables and other items.

Crafting turns resources and refined materials into finished items. Visit the appropriate crafting station, select an item, provide the required materials and pay the crafting fee. Crafting grants fame toward the relevant crafting specialization. Some crafting stations are found in cities, while others can be built on personal or guild islands.

Check the marketplace price of an item before crafting it. Include material costs, station fees, marketplace taxes and transport costs when calculating profit. Compare city crafting bonuses before choosing a station. Start with a small number of item types so you can develop useful crafting specialization.
Refining
Convert raw resources into refined materials such as bars, planks, cloth and leather.

Refining transforms gathered resources into materials used for crafting. For example, ore becomes metal bars, logs become planks, fiber becomes cloth and hide becomes leather. Each material requires the appropriate refining station, resources and a silver fee. Refining also grants fame toward its corresponding specialization.

Compare refining fees between cities before processing large quantities. Cities have different refining bonuses for particular resources, which can improve resource return rates. Check the price of raw and refined materials before deciding whether to refine or sell them directly.
Focus Points
Understand Focus Points and how they improve crafting and refining efficiency.

Focus Points regenerate over time and can be spent on eligible crafting and refining activities. Using focus improves resource return rates, meaning some materials can be returned instead of consumed. Your specialization affects how efficiently you use focus, so higher specialization can make each focus point more valuable.

Avoid spending focus without checking the value of the materials you expect to recover. Compare the cost of materials with the value of the returned resources. Focus is limited, so prioritise activities where it creates the greatest economic benefit. Remember that focus efficiency improves as your relevant specialization increases.
Crafting Specialization
Develop specific crafting professions to improve production efficiency and focus usage.

Crafting items grants fame toward their associated crafting lines. As you gain fame, you unlock higher specialization levels. Specialization improves your ability to craft that item line and can increase resource return efficiency when using focus.

Concentrate on a few item lines that have consistent demand. Check the Destiny Board to see which specializations support your goals. Avoid crafting items at a loss just to gain fame unless you have calculated the cost and consider the progression worthwhile.
Open World PvE
Defeat open-world creatures and mobs to earn fame, silver and loot.

Open-world mobs are found throughout Albion\'s maps. Defeating them grants combat fame and can provide silver, loot and other rewards. Different zones contain different enemy types and difficulty levels. Some areas also have enchanted mobs or special encounters that can offer better rewards.

Choose enemies that match your equipment and experience. Use a build with a balance of damage and sustain so you can keep farming without returning to town too often. Watch for other players, especially in Red and Black Zones, and avoid fighting mobs when you are already low on health.
Solo Dungeons
Explore solo dungeons, defeat their enemies and collect the rewards at the end.

Solo dungeons contain groups of PvE enemies and a final boss. Enter the dungeon, clear its rooms and defeat the boss to receive loot and fame. Dungeon entrances can appear in different zones, and the risk depends on the zone where the dungeon is located.

Bring enough damage and healing to handle the boss. Learn enemy attack patterns and save defensive abilities for dangerous attacks. Use an affordable build when entering full-loot zones. Be aware that other players may find or enter your dungeon before its entrance disappears.
Group Dungeons
Work with a party to clear challenging PvE dungeons and defeat powerful bosses.

Group dungeons are designed for parties and usually require players to work together in different roles. A typical group includes a tank, healer and damage dealers. The group clears enemy packs and bosses while managing positioning, threat and incoming damage.

Agree on roles before entering. Let the tank gather and control enemies, while damage dealers follow the group\'s target priorities. Avoid standing in dangerous attacks and pay attention to the healer\'s position. Bring equipment appropriate for your role and communicate before difficult boss encounters.
Avalonian Dungeons
Take on challenging Avalonian PvE encounters that require preparation and group coordination.

Avalonian dungeons are challenging group PvE activities featuring powerful enemies and encounter mechanics. Players need a coordinated party with suitable roles to clear the dungeon. Successful groups must manage enemy abilities, positioning and boss mechanics rather than relying only on damage.

Prepare your group composition before entering and make sure everyone understands their role. Learn the mechanics of each encounter and communicate dangerous attacks. Bring suitable equipment and consumables, and avoid rushing into unfamiliar boss fights without understanding their mechanics.
Hellgates
Fight through PvE encounters and compete against other players in Hellgate activities.

Hellgates are instanced combat activities that combine PvE enemies with the possibility of PvP encounters. Players clear enemies and may encounter an opposing team. Hellgates come in different formats and group sizes, with different rules and levels of risk.

Prepare for both PvE and PvP. Choose a build with useful damage, mobility and defensive abilities. Coordinate with your teammates and communicate enemy positions and cooldowns. Understand the Hellgate format before entering so you know what to expect.
Open World Solo PvP
Find and fight other players alone in Albion\'s open world.

Open-world solo PvP takes place in areas where players can attack one another. You may encounter opponents while travelling, gathering or farming fame. Fights depend on your build, positioning, equipment and ability to judge whether an engagement is favourable.

Use a build with a combination of damage, mobility and survivability. Check your surroundings before engaging and avoid fighting multiple opponents alone. Learn when to use defensive abilities and when to disengage. In full-loot zones, bring equipment you can afford to replace.
Corrupted Dungeons
Enter solo dungeons where PvE progression can lead to a one-versus-one PvP fight.

Corrupted Dungeons combine solo PvE with solo PvP. You clear enemies, collect rewards and destroy crystals. Another player may invade your dungeon, creating a one-versus-one fight. The dungeon\'s difficulty level determines its risk and reward structure.

Learn the differences between Hunter, Stalker and Slayer difficulty before choosing where to play. Build around your preferred fighting style and learn how your abilities interact with common opponent builds. Understand the crystal objectives and decide whether to fight or defend them based on your situation.
Solo PvP Builds
Learn how to choose weapons, armor and abilities for effective solo PvP.

A solo PvP build usually includes a weapon, off-hand if applicable, headpiece, chest armor, shoes, cape, food and potion. Each piece contributes abilities and bonuses. The best combination depends on the activity, your budget and the playstyle you want to use.

Choose a build you can afford to replace and practise with it before risking expensive equipment. Learn your weapon\'s damage combos, defensive options and mobility. Consider how your build performs against different opponents rather than focusing only on its damage output.
Solo PvP Tips
Improve decision-making, positioning and combat awareness when fighting alone.

Solo PvP rewards players who understand their own abilities and recognise their opponent\'s strengths and weaknesses. Good positioning, cooldown management and timing can decide a fight. Knowing when not to engage is also an important part of surviving.

Inspect opponents when possible and learn to recognise common weapon abilities. Avoid wasting defensive cooldowns and look for opportunities after your opponent uses theirs. Keep an escape option available when travelling through dangerous zones. Review lost fights to understand what you could improve.
Small-Scale PvP
Fight in coordinated small groups where positioning and teamwork are essential.

Small-scale PvP involves fights between relatively small groups of players. Teams combine damage, healing, crowd control and defensive abilities. Success depends on target selection, positioning and using abilities together rather than acting independently.

Communicate targets and important cooldowns. Focus damage on the same opponent and protect your healer. Avoid spreading damage across several enemies without a plan. Stay close enough to support your team while avoiding enemy area attacks.
Group Ganking
Hunt players in open-world zones using coordinated movement, mobility and crowd control.

Ganking groups travel through open-world zones looking for players to catch and kill. Members use mobility, dismount pressure, crowd control and damage to prevent targets from escaping. Different players may take roles such as scout, dismount support or damage dealer.

Coordinate your movement and communicate target locations. Use scouts where possible and avoid chasing targets too far from your group. Make sure your group has enough crowd control to stop escapes. Watch for counter-ganks and do not become careless after finding a target.
Group Hellgates
Compete in team-based Hellgate encounters that combine PvE and organised PvP.

Group Hellgates place teams into an instanced environment where they clear PvE enemies and may fight another team. Group size and rules depend on the Hellgate type. Team composition, target selection and coordinated ability use are important to success.

Agree on your team composition and roles before entering. Focus the same target and communicate defensive cooldowns. Learn how your team handles enemy crowd control and burst damage. Practise together so that your group can react quickly during fights.
Group PvP Builds
Understand group roles and how equipment choices support a coordinated team.

Group PvP builds are designed around team roles such as tank, healer, damage dealer and support. Each role contributes something different to the group. A team\'s overall composition should provide enough damage, healing, crowd control and defensive utility.

Choose your equipment based on the group\'s strategy rather than individual preference alone. Make sure the team has the roles it needs and that players understand their responsibilities. Practise ability combinations and agree on target priorities before entering fights.
Open-World Camps
Clear camps and enemy groups in the open world to earn fame and rewards.

Open-world camps contain groups of enemies and sometimes special objectives or chests. Players defeat the enemies to clear the camp and gain fame, silver and possible loot. The rewards and difficulty depend on the camp and the zone where it appears.

Check the surrounding area before starting, especially in dangerous zones. Use a build that can clear enemy groups efficiently without losing too much health. Watch for other players who may contest the camp and leave if the risk becomes too high.
Outposts
Capture and contest open-world outposts while competing with other players.

Outposts are capturable objectives in the open world. Players generally need to defeat defenders and remain in control of the objective to capture it. Outposts can be contested by other players, so controlling one may lead to PvP encounters.

Check the area for enemy players before committing to a capture. Be ready to defend the objective and avoid becoming isolated. If the area becomes heavily contested, consider regrouping rather than repeatedly entering a fight without support.
Open-World Objectives
Discover chests, objectives and points of interest that can reward exploration and competition.

Open-world maps contain different objectives, including chests, special encounters and points that players can contest. Some objectives reward players for defeating enemies, while others require capturing or controlling a location. The exact mechanics depend on the objective.

Understand the objective before committing your time and equipment. Check the map and nearby activity, and be aware that other players may be approaching. Consider the potential reward against the risk of being attacked or losing your equipment.
Guild Warfare
Learn how guilds organise players, coordinate battles and compete for strategic control.

Guild warfare involves organised groups competing for strategic objectives and influence. Guilds coordinate players into roles and groups, often following instructions from a shot-caller or leader. Preparation, communication and a clear strategy are essential during large-scale battles.

Follow your guild\'s shot-caller and make sure you understand your role before a fight. Prepare the requested equipment and consumables in advance. Stay with your group, communicate important information and avoid using major abilities without coordination.
Territories
Understand territory control and its strategic importance to guilds in the Outlands.

Territories are strategic locations in the Outlands that guilds can control. They are important for guild presence and strategic operations. Territory control can involve organised objectives and battles, with the rules depending on the current territory warfare system.

Learn your guild\'s territory strategy and understand the objectives involved. Coordinate with guild members and prepare the correct equipment before participating. Follow instructions during fights and keep track of enemy movements around important locations.
Castles
Explore castle objectives and learn how groups compete to capture and control them.

Castles are large open-world objectives that groups can contest. Capturing a castle involves fighting defenders and securing its objective. Castles can attract multiple groups, making positioning and coordination important during an engagement.

Bring a coordinated group and follow the caller\'s instructions. Pay attention to enemy positioning and avoid entering a large fight alone. Prepare your equipment beforehand and communicate when your group needs to regroup or reposition.
Faction Warfare
Enlist with a city faction, capture objectives and fight opposing factions for rewards.

Faction Warfare allows players to enlist with a city faction and participate in fights against rival factions. Players can capture faction objectives, escort or contest activities and earn faction points. Faction activities take place in designated areas and may involve open-world PvP.

Choose a faction and learn where its objectives are located. Joining other faction players can make objectives easier to capture and defend. Watch for opposing faction groups and understand the risks of the zone before bringing valuable equipment.
Crystal League
Take part in organised team PvP matches that reward coordination and competitive skill.

Crystal League is a structured team PvP activity in which teams compete under specific match rules. Players use coordinated builds and strategies to defeat the opposing team. Team composition, target selection and timing are important throughout a match.

Practise with the same team when possible. Make sure everyone understands their role, target priorities and defensive responsibilities. Communicate cooldowns and adapt your strategy to the opposing team\'s composition.
Marketplace
Buy and sell items while learning how supply, demand and city prices affect the economy.

The marketplace allows players to buy and sell equipment, resources and other items. You can purchase items through existing sell orders or place buy orders. When selling, you can create a sell order or use an existing buy order. Prices vary between cities and change with player supply and demand.

Compare buy and sell prices before making a trade. Include marketplace taxes and listing fees in your calculations. Avoid investing all your silver in one item and check whether an item sells regularly before buying large quantities. Remember that displayed prices do not guarantee that an item will sell at that price.
Transporting Goods
Move items between cities to take advantage of price differences and market demand.

Transporting involves buying items in one city and moving them to another city where they may sell for a higher price. Profit depends on the difference between market prices after fees and travel costs. The route and mount you choose affect both travel time and risk.

Calculate the expected profit before travelling. Include taxes, listing fees and the possibility that prices may change before you sell. Use a mount with enough carrying capacity and consider safer routes when transporting valuable goods. Avoid carrying more value than you can afford to lose.
Personal Islands
Develop a personal island with buildings, farms and facilities that support your activities.

Personal islands provide private space where players can build facilities and manage certain economic activities. Depending on the buildings and upgrades available, islands can support farming, crafting and other forms of production. Buildings and plots require silver and resources to develop.

Plan your island around the activities you actually intend to use. Compare the cost of buildings and upkeep with the value they provide. Farming and crafting can require regular attention, so consider whether the time and investment fit your playstyle.
Making Silver
Discover different ways to earn, manage and protect your silver in Albion Online.

Silver is Albion\'s main currency and can be earned through many activities, including PvE, gathering, crafting, refining, trading and selling items. Different methods require different levels of investment, time and risk. Your most profitable activity depends on your skills, equipment and the current market.

Track your income and expenses so you know whether an activity is profitable. Avoid buying equipment you cannot afford to replace, especially for full-loot activities. Compare different ways of earning silver and focus on methods that suit your experience and available time.
